questions.key_step: Terms of a G.P. as sides of a triangle; greatest integer: reduce triangle inequality to r^2-r-1<0, so 1<r<(1+sqrt5)/2
questions.justification: Short chain: triangle inequality on the two smaller sides, one quadratic inequality, then floor of r and of -r (needs care with the negative).

questions.key_step: Newton/recurrence S_{n+2}=7S_{n+1}+S_n applied three times (or alpha*beta=-1 shortcut) to collapse the ratio to S2=51
questions.justification: Routine power-sum recurrence; the only skill is spotting that the ratio collapses; numerical format.

questions.key_step: Symmetric/skew-symmetric counting: S2 empty (no zero in S), diagonal triples summing to 0 give 12, then inclusion-exclusion with S1 intersect S3
questions.justification: Needs three counts (S1, S3 via diagonal triples, S1 and S3) and an inclusion-exclusion with an empty S2; many small places to slip but each idea is standard.
